artworks.title: S. Hieronymus in Deserto (Saint Jerome in the Desert)
artworks.artist: Johannes and Lucas van Doetechum after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: This image depicts an expansive landscape viewed from an elevated perspective. The horizon shows distant mountains and a cityscape etched against the sky. The artwork uses intricate linework characteristic of etching to create detailed textures in the clouds and terrain. The color palette is monochromatic, with shades of sepia and brown. In the foreground, a figure rests under a tree surrounded by foliage and rocks. Further back, a river, fields, and a castle on a hill are visible. The sky is filled with layered clouds.

artworks.title: Prospectus Tyburtinus (View of the Tiber)
artworks.artist: Johannes and Lucas van Doetechum after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: The image shows a landscape with a medieval town surrounded by rugged terrain. The town is clustered with a tall tower. A river winds through rocky outcrops in the foreground. The fine and detailed linework depicts the buildings and natural formations. The color palette is primarily gray. The background features hills and structures fading into the distance, creating depth and space. The composition blends the built and natural environments with precision.

artworks.title: Pagus Nemorosus (Wooded Village)
artworks.artist: Johannes and Lucas van Doetechum after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.medium: etching and engraving on laid paper
artworks.description: The image shows a rural village landscape from an elevated perspective. The horizon is high in the composition beneath clouds, and a church spire is visible in the distance among trees. A detailed woodland scene is depicted, with trees and a horse-drawn covered wagon on a path. People are shown near the path. The color palette is monochromatic in shades of beige and dark brown, typical of detailed etchings or engravings.

artworks.title: River Landscape with the Fall of Icarus
artworks.artist: Attributed to Simon Novellanus after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.medium: etching and engraving on laid paper
artworks.description: This print depicts land and water from an elevated perspective. A mountain or large hill dominates the distant horizon. Numerous sailboats are on the river below, and the river winds towards distant hills and buildings. Above, within a swirl of clouds, two people appear to be falling from the sky above. One of the people has large wings, and the other is surrounded by feathers. At the bottom of the print are several lines of text.

artworks.title: The Parable of the Good Shepherd
artworks.artist: Philip Galle after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a pastoral scene with various figures and animals. The central figure stands in a doorway holding a sheep, surrounded by other animals. There are groups of figures shown attempting to intrude, working on the roof, and herding sheep in the background. The style of the drawing is reminiscent of intricate engravings from the Northern Renaissance.

artworks.title: The Triumph of Time
artworks.artist: Philip Galle after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: This print shows several people and animals in a complex landscape. In the center, a man in a tunic is seated on an hourglass on top of a chariot, looking over his shoulder to the left. In one hand he holds a child up to his mouth, and in the other he holds a thin hoop made of a snake eating its own tail. He has a boot on one foot, while the other is bare. He is surrounded by a circle containing the twelve symbols of the zodiac, some hanging from a tree that grows out of the circle. On the left, there is an angelic figure blowing a horn atop an elephant, and a skeleton with a scythe rides a donkey nearby. On the right, two horses drag the chariot, one with the shape of the sun on its back and the other with a crescent moon. The background includes a detailed landscape with thin trees, hills, a body of water, and buildings, including a church steeple and windmills. The ground beneath the procession is littered with objects such as pieces of armor, tools, instruments, books, chests, and clothes. Below the print are several lines of text.

artworks.title: The Battle of the Moneybags and the Strongboxes
artworks.artist: Pieter van der Heyden after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: Printed with fine black lines and hatching, creatures made of fabric sacks with human heads, arms, and legs and wooden chests and barrels with limbs are all dressed in armor and battle in this horizontal engraving. Spears, lances, and swords pierce bags and chests alike, and coins spill out of many of them. The characters are crowded as they fight in front of a couple of puffs of smoke in the background to the right and a sea of upright spears to the left. The fighting is confused, with severed limbs lying about and one soldier fighting with a dagger slicing his helmet. A printed signature in the lower right corner reads, P. Bruegel Inuet, Ioan Galle excudit.” An inscription in the bottom center of the image reads, “DIVITLAE FACIVNT FVRES. Multos perdidit aurem et argenium, Eccli 8.5. LES RICHESSES FONT DES LARRONS. L'or et l'argent en a destruit plusieurs. RYCKDOM MAECKT DIEVEN./ Goudt en silver heeft vek bedrove.” Text in three columns under the image reads, “Quid modo diuitie, quid fului vasta metalli Congeries, nummis arca referta nouis, Illecebres inter tantas, atq agmina furum, Inditium cunctis efferus vncus erit, Preda facit furem, feruens mala cuncta ministrat, Impetus, et spolijs apta rapina feris. Wel aen ghij Spaerpotten, Tonnen, en Kisten. Tis al om gelt en goet, dit striden en twisten. Al seet men u ooc anders, willet niet ghelouen. Daerom vueren wij den haec die ons noijt en miste. Men soeckt wel actie om ons te uerdoouen, Maer men souwer niet krijgen, waerder niet te rooven.”

artworks.title: The Last Judgment
artworks.artist: Pieter van der Heyden after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a scene depicting a central figure on a cloud surrounded by angelic figures blowing trumpets. Below them, there are various figures being herded onto boats, with strange creatures around. On one side, monstrous figures are present, while on the opposite side, the figures flow out of a giant egg-like form. Many people are shown in lines, with fantastical creatures throughout the image. The composition contrasts between the celestial peace above and the chaotic scene below.

artworks.title: Anger
artworks.artist: Pieter van der Heyden after Pieter Bruegel the Elder

artworks.title: Avarice
artworks.artist: Pieter van der Heyden after Pieter Bruegel the Elder

artworks.title: Envy
artworks.artist: Pieter van der Heyden after Pieter Bruegel the Elder

artworks.title: Gluttony
artworks.artist: Pieter van der Heyden after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: The image shows swirling and curving lines with scattered figures of different shapes throughout. It features a dream-like scene with peculiar and abstract imagery. In the upper left section, a face emerges from a barrel with wheels. Nearby, a table is filled with twisted human forms interacting in a chaotic manner. On the right, a head with windmill sails protrudes from a mound, with oversized barrels in the landscape. Various figures engage in activities like climbing and resting within the narrative of the environment.

artworks.title: Lust
artworks.artist: Pieter van der Heyden after Pieter Bruegel the Elder

artworks.title: Pride
artworks.artist: Pieter van der Heyden after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: This is a print showing a chaotic scene featuring strange creatures and oddly-shapes structures. Some of the structures in the background seem to emit smoke or vapor, as do some hills behind them. The creatures that fill the scene seem to have a combination of human and animal characteristics and exaggerated proportions. Several of the creatures seem to be looking at their reflections in mirrors of different sizes, and many also appear to be grooming themselves or others. To the right of center, a peacock walks alongside several of these creatures. At the bottom of the print are several lines of text.

artworks.title: Sloth
artworks.artist: Pieter van der Heyden after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: The image contains swirling lines and organic shapes to create an abstract composition. There is a clock with a pointed pendulum in the center. The scene resembles a chaotic village with winding paths and creatures that blend human and animal characteristics. These include snail-like figures with human heads, a boat with a bird's face, and a fish-shaped structure. Hybrid figures reminiscent of mythical creatures are engaged in leisurely activities.

artworks.title: The Witch of Malleghem
artworks.artist: Pieter van der Heyden after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a densely packed scene with various figures and objects. The scene depicts fantastical characters engaged in different activities around tables with jugs and cups. The environment is lively with intricate details in each figure's attire and expression. There are oversized fruit, baskets, ladders, buildings in the distance, and ships in the background. Objects include a devilish creature on a barrel and a figure crouched in a large egg, adding ambiguity and humor. This illustration is reminiscent of works by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, with a whimsical and complex composition creating a narrative richness.

artworks.title: The Witch of Malleghem
artworks.artist: Pieter van der Heyden after Pieter Bruegel the Elder

artworks.title: Epileptics Walking to the Right
artworks.artist: Hendrik Hondius I after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: The image shows six men walking closely together in a line. They are standing and walking forward, holding onto each other's arms or shoulders. Their facial expressions are varied, with different features such as closed eyes, squinting, mouths slightly open, long noses, and furrowed brows. Their hair ranges from short to long and disheveled. They are dressed in long robes and simple attire like tunics, pants, and shoes, without any visible jewelry or objects. The background features a natural setting with trees of varying heights, a path leading into the distance, and a small countryside scene with structures resembling houses or barns. The landscape extends to show distant silhouettes of buildings or towers, suggesting a rural environment.

artworks.title: A Dutch Hulk and a Boeier
artworks.artist: Frans Huys and Cornelis Cort? after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: The image displays a detailed engraving of a seascape with a large ship at the center. The perspective shows the sea, ships, and distant city structures. The artwork features intricate line work in shades of brown and beige, highlighting textures and patterns. Waves surround the ships, and dramatic clouds fill the sky.

artworks.title: The Fat Kitchen
artworks.artist: anonymous Netherlandish 17th Century engraver, after Pieter van der Heyden, after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.dimensions: sheet (trimmed to plate mark): 21.8 x 28.2 cm (8 9/16 x 11 1/8 in.)

artworks.title: Christ and the Adultress
artworks.artist: Pieter Perret after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: The image shows a group of people gathered around a central figure who is kneeling on the ground. The figure is seen from head to toe, kneeling forward with one hand extended towards the ground, with facial features partially visible beneath a hood and long flowing hair. The central figure's head is tilted down, gazing at a spot on the ground where there are writings. He is dressed in a long robe that covers most of his body. To his left stands a female figure, visible from head to toe, wearing a long dress that accentuates her waist, holding her hands together in front of her. Surrounding them is a crowd of men and women, some in long robes, some with hats or head coverings. They exhibit varied expressions and postures, with one leaning forward with a stick pointing towards the ground. The background consists of a dense assembly of people with indistinct architectural elements visible beyond them.

artworks.title: The Misanthrope Robbed by the World
artworks.artist: Johan Wierix after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: The image depicts a robed figure and a person trapped inside a sphere. The central feature shows a hooded figure walking in front of a windmill, while a smaller figure is partially caught in a round object with a sword protruding from it. The smaller figure reaches towards the larger figure. In the background, various figures are engaged in dynamic interactions, such as a cart with horses and soldiers, indicating motion and activity. The landscape includes hills and clouds in the sky, contributing to the mood. There is ornate script in an older language around the central circle, potentially conveying an allegorical or moral message.

artworks.title: The Archbishop Blessing the Child after the Baptism
artworks.artist: Hans Burgkmair I
artworks.dimensions: sheet (trimmed to image): 22.1 x 19.7 cm (8 11/16 x 7 3/4 in.)
artworks.description: The image shows several individuals in an ornate architectural setting with arches and columns. In the center, a person with a crown and long garments holds a child wrapped in cloth. To the left, a group of people wearing various hats and cloaks engage with the central figures. On the right, another individual wears a decorative floral hat and detailed outfit. The figures appear to be interacting, with one figure to the left holding a staff. Above them, through the arches, there are depictions of trees or foliage adding detail to the background, which features an intricately designed ceiling or entablature.

artworks.title: The Archbishop Blessing the Child after the Baptism
artworks.artist: Hans Burgkmair I
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a group of figures standing in an architectural setting. The image shows detailed lines illustrating figures dressed in ornate garments, in an interior with pillars and arches. Each figure wears richly textured robes, hats, and capes. The dense line work and intricate details add depth to the garments and setting. The figures are positioned in a way that suggests a narrative scene within a historical or biblical context.
